children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

recently_moved_to_uk.description: Whether the claimant has recently moved to the UK.

right_to_reside_status.description: A plain English description of the claimant's right-to-reside position.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are there?** (Please also tell me their names or what you'd like to call them for this conversation.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my daughter Alex. She's 3 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 3 years old and lives with you in the UK.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you currently living in the UK yourself?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am living in the UK. I've actually just recently moved here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming. Since you've recently moved to the UK, I need to ask:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, do you have British citizenship, settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live here?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about my right-to-reside position, to be honest. It's all quite complicated with the move being so recent. I'm still trying to work out all the paperwork and what my exact status is.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - immigration status can be quite complex, especially after a recent move.

The right to reside is an important factor in determining eligibility for Child Benefit. Since you're unsure about your status, let me ask a few questions that might help clarify:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have citizenship from another country? If from another country, which one?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all those details right now if that's okay. Like I said, I've just moved here recently and I'm still working through understanding my exact right-to-reside position. Is there anything else you need to know about my situation to help me understand if I might be eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand, and that's okay. Let me ask about a few other aspects of your situation:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or family member?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care - meaning you're the one providing for her needs like food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm fully responsible for Alex. I take care of all her needs - her food, clothes, everything she needs day-to-day.
